correctness.rationale: For distinct indices \(i,j\), the symmetric difference of the closed neighborhoods of \(a_i\) and \(a_j\) is exactly the union of the two deleted-matching pairs \(P_i\) and \(P_j\). Hence at most one pair can be omitted and every identifying code has size at least \(n-1\). Equality forces one omitted pair and one selected vertex in every other pair. The displayed trace formulas then prove necessity and sufficiency of at least two selected vertices on each side, and direct binomial summation gives \(n(2^{n-1}-2n)\). Quantifiers are for all integers \(n\ge5\). The exhaustive verifier through \(n=9\) agrees but is corroborative only.
